results.question: According to TPS_ECUR_01015, what is the primary goal of the ECU Resource Template regarding Basic Software configuration?
results.answer: The primary goal of the ECU Resource Template, as stated in TPS_ECUR_01015, is to support the configuration of the AUTOSAR Basic Software by providing information on the respective hardware and on how the hardware is connected to each other. [1]

citations.excerpt: General Hardware Description The ECU Resource Template utilizes the basic building blocks • hardware elements • hierarchies of hardware elements • hardware pins • hardware pin groups • hardware connections to describe the relevant aspects of the actual hardware. The ECU Resource Template allows however to choose the appropriate level of detail in the description of the hard- ware, depending on the use case. It also allows to describe arbitrary hardware and its connections. results.question: According to constraint constr_3512, what restriction applies to the multiple instantiation of hardware elements?
results.answer: According to constraint constr_3512, a hardware element may not be instantiated more than once. Each HwElement can be the target of only a single nestedElement reference; therefore, if the same hardware element is required in several places, each occurrence must be described by a distinct HwElement clone, along with cloned structural features such as pin groups, pins, and connections. The same HwType may still be referenced by multiple HwElement clones, but the element itself cannot be reused without cloning its description. [1][2]

E.g. the CPU is described by a Semiconductor-Vendor, the project specific usage of such a CPU is described by the ECU vendor. [constr_3512] No support of multiple instantiation ⌈ An essential constraint is that each HwElement can only be target of one nestedElement reference. This means that there is no concept of multiple instantiation of hardware elements. If the same hardware element shall be used several times (using the nestedElement reference) each occurrence has to have its own description. This is also true for nested elements of the referenced nested element. ⌋ () Thus the hardware element and all its structural features (hardware pin groups, hard- ware pins and hardware connections) need to be cloned. There is however the possi- bility to reference the same HwType from several HwElement clones.

results.question: What is the purpose of HwPinGroup and where can an HwPinGroup exist inside?
results.answer: The **HwPinGroup** is a meta‑class that represents a bundle of hardware pins used to describe dedicated connectivity channels for hardware elements. It can model grouped hardware ports such as ADC and DIO, structure port information hierarchically, and at the detailed level describe individual hardware pins. An **HwPinGroup** may only be contained inside a **HwElement** or nested within another **HwPinGroup**. [2]

citations.excerpt: 2.4 Hardware Pin and Pin Group The HwPinGroup allows to describe dedicated channels of connectivity for hardware elements. It can be used to describe grouped hardware ports like ADC and DIO. It can structure the port information hierarchically. At the detailed level it can be used to describe individual hardware pins. Each HwPinGroup is Identifiable . A HwPinGroup can only exist inside a HwEle- ment or another HwPinGroup . Each HwPinGroup inherits from HwDescriptionEntity and is therefore capable to describe a set of attributes (see section 2.1 for details). The content of the HwPinGroup is aggregated in the role hwPinGroupContent . Class HwPinGroup Package M2::AUTOSARTemplates::EcuResourceTemplate Note This meta-class represents the ability to describe groups of pins which are used to connect hardware elements. This group acts as a bundle of pins. Thereby they allow to describe high level connections. Pin groups can even be nested. The ele- ments contained in the HwPinGroupContent ( HwPinGroup and HwPin ) can occur in an arbitrary order and multiple times. results.question: According to constraint constr_3513, what features may a hardware connection connect?
results.answer: According to constraint constr_3513, a hardware connection may connect only features that are both within the hierarchical scope of the hardware element that contains the connection. The hierarchical scope includes all features belonging to that hardware element and all features belonging to hardware elements that are referenced directly or indirectly through the nestedElement relation from that element. [3]

citations.excerpt: [constr_3513] Scope of connections ⌈ Each hardware connection shall only connect features which both are in the hierarchical scope of the hardware element. The hierar- chical scope encloses • all features belonging to the hardware element containing the connection • all features belonging to hardware elements which are referenced directly and indirectly in the nestedElement relation from the hardware element containing connection. ⌋ () Especially it is allowed to specify connections in hardware elements which are in deeper hierarchical level and also connections which cross hierarchical levels. In the example from figure B.1 the following connections are allowed: • connections specified in the scope of hardware element "MyEcu" – all the shown connections can be specified on this level – even the connections inside another hierarchical hardware element (e.g. be- tween "Pu1" and "Can") can be specified on this level – even the connections crossing hierarchical levels (e.g. between "Can" and "Trcv") can be specified on this level • connections specified in the scope of hardware element "MicroController" – only the connections inside the hardware element "MicroController" (e.g. be- tween "Pu1" and "Can") can be specified.

results.question: According to TPS_BSWMDT_04073, which package is the meta-class ExclusiveArea imported from, and what is its purpose?
results.answer: According to TPS_BSWMDT_04073, the meta‑class **ExclusiveArea** is imported from the **CommonStructure** package of the meta‑model (M2::AUTOSARTemplates::CommonStructure::InternalBehavior) [1]. Its purpose is to define a region in which an executable entity is protected from preemption, thereby preventing the entity from being interrupted while it runs within that exclusive area [1].
